intro: A protest song written in winter 1962–63, set to an old tune. He has kept it in the set for six decades, often in arrangements that sound nothing like the original.

lives.title: Nottamun Town
lives.note: The melody comes from "Nottamun Town" as arranged by the Kentucky folk singer Jean Ritchie. His lawyers later settled with her.

lives.title: Town Hall
lives.note: One of the early concert performances, at his first major New York hall show.

lives.title: Freewheelin'
lives.note: Voice and guitar, harsh and steady. On The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan.

lives.title: The Grammys, during the Gulf War
lives.place: Radio City Music Hall, New York
lives.note: Accepting a lifetime achievement award, he played it fast and loud with a band, the words hard to make out — a choice many saw as a comment on the war.

others.note: At the 30th anniversary concert in Madison Square Garden.
